scenes.say: In nineteen twenty-five, a man sold the Eiffel Tower. Then he came back, and sold it again.
scenes.cap: In 1925, a man SOLD the Eiffel Tower. Then he came back... and sold it AGAIN.

scenes.say: His name was Victor Lustig. One of the greatest con men who ever lived.
scenes.cap: His name was VICTOR LUSTIG. One of the greatest CON MEN who ever lived.

scenes.say: He read that the tower was rusting, and costly to repaint. That gave him an idea.
scenes.cap: He read that the tower was RUSTING, and costly to repaint. That gave him an IDEA.

scenes.say: He faked government papers, and invited a group of scrap metal dealers to a luxury hotel in Paris.
scenes.cap: He FAKED government papers, and invited SCRAP METAL dealers to a luxury hotel in Paris.

scenes.say: His story? The city would sell the tower for scrap. And it was top secret.
scenes.cap: His story? The city would sell the tower for SCRAP. And it was TOP SECRET.

scenes.say: One dealer, André Poisson, wanted it badly. But his wife was suspicious.
scenes.cap: One dealer, André Poisson, wanted it BADLY. But his wife was SUSPICIOUS.

scenes.say: So Lustig confessed. He said he was a corrupt official, and he needed a bribe.
scenes.cap: So Lustig CONFESSED. He said he was a corrupt official, and he needed a BRIBE.

scenes.say: And that made it believable. Poisson paid for the tower. And the bribe.
scenes.cap: And that made it BELIEVABLE. Poisson paid for the tower. And the BRIBE.

scenes.say: Lustig jumped on a train to Vienna with the cash.
scenes.cap: Lustig jumped on a train to VIENNA with the CASH.

scenes.say: And Poisson? He was too embarrassed to go to the police.
scenes.cap: And Poisson? He was too EMBARRASSED to go to the police.

scenes.say: So Lustig came back, and tried it again. This time, a dealer called the police. And Lustig escaped.
scenes.cap: So Lustig came back and tried it AGAIN. This time, a dealer called the POLICE. And Lustig ESCAPED.

scenes.say: Years later, he was caught in America for counterfeiting money, and sent to Alcatraz.
scenes.cap: Years later, he was caught in America for COUNTERFEITING, and sent to ALCATRAZ.

scenes.say: The man who sold the Eiffel Tower. Follow Paper Trail, for the money stories nobody tells you.
scenes.cap: The man who sold the EIFFEL TOWER. Follow PAPER TRAIL for the money stories nobody tells you.

In 1925, con man Victor Lustig posed as a French government official and 'sold' the Eiffel Tower to a scrap metal dealer. Then he came back and tried it again.
